The bull case rests on third quarter revenue of $1.85 billion, up 36% from a year earlier and up 7.51% from the quarter before [D1]. Net income of $397 million was up 107.85% from a year earlier, and net margin was 21.51% [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group contributed $1.35 billion of revenue, up 43.09%, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group contributed $501 million, up 21.60% [D1]. Segment operating income of $613 million was up 81.36% from a year earlier [D1]. Orders made a second consecutive record quarter [D1]. Management said AI infrastructure demand is far exceeding the ability to supply, and the wireline business exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3]. The fourth quarter outlook calls for revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion, about 37% growth at the midpoint, and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on 172 million diluted shares [D1]. The next report needs to see revenue at or above the top end of that guided range and another record order quarter [D1].

The bear case starts with the concentration of the quarter in a single segment, since the Communications Solutions Group produced $1.35 billion of the $1.85 billion in revenue [D1]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible today than a year earlier [D3]. Revenue conversion is expected to be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. The quarter also benefited from one-time tariff impacts that management said will not repeat, which raises the bar for future profitability [D3]. Analysts pressed on whether the current order level is sustainable, and management's own base case is orders only slightly up from the third quarter [D3]. The next report needs to see orders sustained at a record level without a supply driven shortfall in revenue conversion, and profitability that does not rely on the non-repeating tariff benefit [D3].
